summary: Timezone-shifted billing buckets caused microbilling and missing reserved credits for batch jobs
description:
Issue summary:
LogiStat reports small unexpected charges (microbilling) appearing on multiple hourly invoice lines for a single nightly batch job, plus a missing reserved-capacity credit for the same window. The customer runs large nightly batch embedding jobs against a dedicated pool with reserved capacity.

Impact:
- Customer observed 18 distinct 1-5 USD line items over three hours instead of a single consolidated hourly line.
- Reserved capacity credits that should have offset the batch were not applied, resulting in a net unexpected charge of ~$72 on the provisional invoice.
- Affects accounting reconciliation and triggered internal billing alerts for the customer.

Environment:
- Prod, us-west
- Dedicated pool: dc-west-2-reserved-8gpu
- Job: nightly-batch-embeds-logs-2026-03-09 (runs ~02:00-03:30 PDT)

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1. Trigger the same batch via their scheduler (observed on 2026-03-09).
2. Inspect activity in Billing > Usage Explorer for the hour starting 02:00 PDT.
3. Compare line items in provisional invoice for 02:00-05:00 window.

Observed behavior:
- The job's usage was split into multiple micro-buckets that span the 02:00 PDT hour boundary. Each micro-bucket was billed at host rate rather than reserved rate for some microbatches.
- Usage aggregator has multiple short-duration postbacks with timestamps in UTC that were migrated into hour buckets after a timezone offset adjustment.
- Reserved-capacity offset appears only on the consolidated hourly accumulator; because the microbuckets were written with misaligned hour keys, the credit did not match and was not applied.

Expected behavior:
- Batch job usage within the reserved capacity window should aggregate into a single hourly bucket and receive the reserved-capacity credit automatically.

Attachments / logs provided by customer:
- Usage CSV extract for 2026-03-09 02:00-05:00 PDT (attached to case).
- Provisionally generated invoice screenshot showing the multiple small line items.
- Internal scheduler logs showing job start/end times in local timezone.

Initial customer request:
- Please investigate why the reserved-capacity credit did not apply and provide a provisional credit while we investigate reconciliation.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Escalating to billing engineers and SRE. Requested customer's usage CSV and invoice screenshot. Asked for timezone of scheduler (PDT confirmed).

2026-03-10 11:03 - Marcus Nguyen (Billing Eng): Triage complete. Observed postback event timestamps in the customer's CSV are in UTC; our aggregator applied a -7h offset during an interim timezone migration script that ran 2026-03-09 00:50 UTC. Hypothesis: the migration shifted bucket keys for a subset of events, creating out-of-hour microbuckets. Investigating commit and accumulator behavior. Linking PR 4827 for the migration script.

2026-03-10 14:28 - SRE Team (note): We replayed a subset of postbacks in staging and reproduced split hourly buckets when events had mixed timezone metadata. Aggregator will group by hour-key which is computed from event_timestamp after applying acct_time_offset. The offset was inconsistent for events before/after the migration marker.
2026-03-11 08:50 - Customer (LogiStat - E. Ramirez): Thank you. Would appreciate a provisional credit while you confirm root cause — this impacts our monthly close.

2026-03-11 16:30 - Marcus Nguyen (Billing Eng): Provisionally applied credit of $72 to customer account pending final reconciliation (credit memo CM-2026-03-11-772790). Noted in invoice comments. Engineering will produce a postmortem and a fix to skip the migration offset for already-ingested timestamps.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer confirmed they see provisional credit on their billing dashboard. Waiting on eng for permanent fix and roll-forward reconciliation notes.
investigation_notes: Found an intermittent timezone-normalization script (merged via PR 4827) that ran during the customer's job window and adjusted acct_time_offset for live ingest workers.
Events arriving before the script had offset 0, after the script offset -7h; the aggregator computed different hour-keys causing split buckets.
Reserved-capacity credits are looked up by hour-key; non-matching keys prevented application of reserved offset for affected microbuckets.

Replayed 1.2M events in staging: reproduced behavior for events with mixed offset headers. Verified that a migration guard to only apply offset to events with missing timezone metadata fixes grouping.
resolution: Provisionally credited $72 to customer (CM-2026-03-11-772790). Engineering to deploy guard to skip retrospective timezone offseting for events that already include timezone metadata. Final reconciliation to run after fix; customer to be notified with postmortem and any additional credits if needed.
next_steps: ENG: Ship migration-guard patch (target: 2026-03-13 deploy to prod).
BILLING: Re-run hourly accumulator for affected window after patch and reconcile final invoice lines (owner: Marcus Nguyen).
SUPPORT: Send postmortem and confirmation of final credit to customer (owner: Aisha Patel).
